sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File purpose and scope
sections.what: States that the module only changes how Windows spells long paths, and that no system setting is changed. Imports the operating system and path tools it needs.
sections.why: The docstring sets the scope so that reviewers know this is not a general path fixer.

sections.name: native_path
sections.title: Converting a path for Windows
sections.what: On Windows, makes a path absolute and adds the long-path prefix. Paths that start as network shares get the network form of the prefix, and paths that already have a prefix are kept as they are. Other systems get the original path back.
sections.why: Likely reason: links are kept visible on purpose. The comment says resolving would hide the redirect that archive checks must inspect.
sections.watch_out: Do not replace this with a resolve call, since resolving removes the link information that the archive checks rely on.

summary: Adds the Windows long-path prefix to a path when needed, and returns every other path unchanged.
purpose: Lets the package reader open folders and files whose full paths are longer than Windows normally allows, without changing any system setting.
why: The docstring states the scope: the change is limited to these reads, with no registry or location changes.
how: 1. On non-Windows systems, return the path unchanged. 2. On Windows, make the path absolute. 3. Keep it unchanged if it already has the prefix. 4. For network share paths, use the network form of the prefix. 5. Otherwise add the plain long-path prefix.
outputs: A path object with the Windows long-path prefix where needed, or the same path on other systems.
risks: The path is not resolved, so links stay visible to security checks. A wrong prefix makes Windows reject the path. The function does not check that the path exists.
debug: On Windows, if a long path fails, print the returned value and check that it starts with the long-path prefix. On other systems the function never changes the path, so look at the calling code instead.
